about.title: I’m Ajay. I like making the complex make sense.
about.body:
I like understanding the bigger opportunity, making sense of complexity, bringing different perspectives together, and turning an idea into something real. My work sits across product design, intelligent experiences, enterprise systems, identity, and interactive experiences.

I started sketching in school. Drawing came naturally, long before I knew it could become a career. Later, games and digital art opened up a bigger possibility: not just drawing things, but creating the worlds, experiences, and ideas behind them. That became the foundation for how I work today.

Art taught me to see. Games taught me to think in worlds, interactions, and systems. Enterprise taught me to work with complexity, scale, technology, and real business constraints. Design brought those experiences together. I don’t see these as separate disciplines; they help me approach problems from different angles.

A brief is often only the starting point. I look for the problem behind it, the opportunity around it, and what could be better. Products live inside larger ecosystems of people, technology, workflows, and business decisions. I use strategy, prototypes, systems, visual design, and experimentation to turn possibilities into something people can see, challenge, and experience.

I’m currently the design lead for IBM’s Engineering Lifecycle Management portfolio, shaping product design, AI experiences, and innovation across the suite. I also mentor designers and colleagues, and share what I’m learning through talks, internal sessions, and writing.

I’m drawn to difficult problems, ambitious ideas, and thoughtful teams—especially where design can change what’s possible. I’m still exploring what comes next.
